title: What Filipinos can learn from ASEAN Prize 2026 recipient Hla Hla Aung
summary: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations has recognized a Myanmar geologist and seismologist as recipient of this year's ASEAN Prize.

blocks.text: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) has recognized a Myanmar geologist and seismologist as recipient of this year's ASEAN Prize.
Hla Hla Aung was recognized for her continued commitment to advancing disaster resilience, particularly in turning scientific research into policies and community empowerment.
In an interview, Hla Hla Aung shared experiences that Filipinos can learn from regarding earthquake response.
Limited studies on earthquakes? That did not stop Hla Hla Aung from learning and sharing information to help communities.
She, instead, read English articles and then translated these into the Myanmar language.

"I used to read books from the foreign countries, articles written by the foreign experts. Then, I have to use the experience from these books and articles for the Myanmar earthquake," the ASEAN Prize recipient said in an interview.
At 80, Hla Hla Aung still continues her advocacy to promote disaster preparedness and resiliency. MARIEL CELINE SERQUIÑA/GMA News

Hla Hla Aung serves as patron of the Myanmar Earthquake Committee of the Myanmar Engineering Society, which aims to enhance earthquake preparedness, seismic hazard assessment, and structural safety throughout Myanmar.
She did not just stop at learning about earthquakes from foreign studies but also translated her learnings from English to the Myanmar language and published these in local newspapers.
"So if people know about earthquakes, they will build strong houses to avoid the damage during the disaster," Hla Hla Aung said.
For 20 years since 1969, Hla Hla Aung has dedicated herself to advancing disaster resilience, even giving demonstrations at schools and monasteries.
One thing she emphasized during the interview is the importance of duck, cover, and hold.

"I demonstrate. You just hold, cover your head, drop under the table, and then you just hold on the leg of the table or bed, and you stay there until you have help from outside. That's the way," Hla Hla Aung said.
"So, I demonstrate to the monastery students, and to other school," she added.
Now 80 years old, Hla Hla Aung continues her advocacy to push for a disaster resilient community.
"You cannot get this (ASEAN Prize) only one, two, three years [but] 20 years. I'm still doing the same thing," Hla Hla Aung said.
"I'm writing articles because I want people to know what to do when earthquake occurs. Then you can save the lives of the people," she added.
Established in 2018, the ASEAN Prize is an annual regional award that recognizes and celebrates outstanding achievements by ASEAN citizens. —KG, GMA News
